title: Induction Motors — Slip, Speed & Power Flow
subtitle: Induction motors are the workhorses of industry — over 90% of all industrial motors. Rugged, cheap, AC supply direct. The key insight: the rotor never catches the rotating magnetic field. That gap (slip) is what produces torque.

subtopics.title: Slip, Speed, Power Flow & Motor Types

content.text: 3-phase AC in stator → rotating magnetic field at Ns. Field induces EMF in rotor conductors → rotor current → Lorentz force → torque. Rotor chases the field but can never catch it: if N=Ns, no relative motion → no EMF → no current → no torque → rotor slows down. So s is always >0 in normal operation.
Rotor frequency fr = s×f. At standstill (s=1): fr = supply frequency. At normal speed (s=0.04): fr = 2Hz.
Power flow: Air gap power P_ag reaches rotor. Rotor copper loss = s×P_ag. Mechanical power = (1−s)×P_ag. Rotor efficiency = N/Ns = 1−s. Low slip → small rotor copper loss → high efficiency.

SCIM (Squirrel Cage): copper bars short-circuited at ends. Rugged, no maintenance, cheap. Fixed resistance. WRIM (Wound Rotor): full 3-phase winding, external resistance via slip rings. Variable speed and high starting torque at cost of complexity.

items: fr = s × f Rotor copper loss = s × P_ag

content.text: Common mistake — P in Ns=120f/P is total poles, NOT pole pairs. 4-pole motor: P=4, Ns=1500rpm. Using P=2 gives 3000rpm — double the correct answer. Always use total number of poles.
